entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Michael Bourtzes was a prominent Byzantine general who played a pivotal role in the politics and warfare of the late 10th century.

Born into a military family, Bourtzes rose to prominence under Emperor Nikephoros II Phokas, capturing key territories from the Arabs in 969. However, his ambition and sense of grievance led him to join forces with conspirators who assassinated Phokas just weeks later.

Bourtzes' allegiance shifted during the civil war between Basil II and Bardas Skleros, as he alternately supported and opposed the two claimants to the throne. His tumultuous career culminated in a series of brutal battles and power struggles that would shape the fate of the Byzantine Empire.

Despite his fall from favor, Bourtzes' legacy endured, leaving an indelible mark on the history of medieval Europe.
